Splom

Source: vignettes/articles/r-docs/splom.Rmd
splom.Rmd

Splom trace

A scaterplot matrix is a matrix associated to n numerical arrays (data variables), X1,X2,.,XnX^1,X^2,.,X_n , of the same length. The cell (i,j) of such a matrix displays the scatter plot of the variable Xi versus Xj ,

The Plotly splom trace implementation for the scaterplot matrix does not require to set x=Xix=Xi , and y=Xjy=Xj, for each scatter plot. All arrays, X1,X2,.,XnX^1,X^2,.,X_n , are passed once, through a list of go_splom_dimension() objects called dimensions, i.e. each array/variable represents a dimension.

A trace of type splom is defined as follows:

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_splom(
    dimensions = list(
      go_splom_dimension(label = "string-1", values = X1),
      go_splom_dimension(label = "string-2", values = X2),
      .
      .
      .
      go_splom_dimension(label = "string-n", values = Xn)
    ),
    text = text,
    marker = go_splom_marker(...)
  )

The label in each dimension is assigned to the axes titles of the corresponding matrix cell.

text is either a unique string assigned to all points displayed by splom or a list of strings of the same length as the dimensions, XiX_i. The text[k] is the tooltip for the kthk^{th} point in each cell.

marker sets the markers attributes in all scatter plots.

Splom of the Iris data set 

library(plotly.core)

df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/iris-data.csv")

The Iris dataset contains four data variables, sepal length, sepal width, petal length petal width, for 150 iris flowers. The flowers are labeled as Iris-setosa, Iris-versicolor, Iris-virginica.

Define a discrete colorscale with three colors corresponding to the three flower classes:

pl_colorscale <- list(
  c(0.0, "#19d3f3"),
  c(0.333, "#19d3f3"),
  c(0.333, "#e763fa"),
  c(0.666, "#e763fa"),
  c(0.666, "#636efa"),
  c(1, "#636efa")
)

Then create the splom:

xaxis_style <- go_xaxis(
  showline = FALSE,
  zeroline = FALSE,
  gridcolor = "#ffff",
  ticklen = 4
)
yaxis_style <- go_yaxis(
  showline = FALSE,
  zeroline = FALSE,
  gridcolor = "#ffff",
  ticklen = 4
)

dims <- list(
  go_splom_dimension(label = "sepal length", values = ~sepal.length),
  go_splom_dimension(label = "sepal width", values = ~sepal.width),
  go_splom_dimension(label = "petal length", values = ~petal.length),
  go_splom_dimension(label = "petal width", values = ~petal.width)
)

fig <- df |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_splom(
    dimensions = dims,
    text = ~class,
    marker = go_splom_marker(
      color = as.integer(factor(df$class)),
      colorscale = pl_colorscale,
      size = 7,
      line = go_splom_marker_line(
        width = 1,
        color = "rgb(230,230,230)"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Iris Data set",
    hovermode = "closest",
    dragmode = "select",
    plot_bgcolor = "rgba(240,240,240, 0.95)",
    xaxis = xaxis_style,
    yaxis = yaxis_style,
    xaxis2 = xaxis_style,
    xaxis3 = xaxis_style,
    xaxis4 = xaxis_style,
    yaxis2 = yaxis_style,
    yaxis3 = yaxis_style,
    yaxis4 = yaxis_style
  )

fig

The scatter plots on the principal diagonal can be removed by setting diagonal = go_splom_diagonal(visible = FALSE):

library(plotly.core)

fig2 <- fig |>
  update_traces(diagonal = go_splom_diagonal(visible = FALSE))

fig2

To plot only the lower/upper half of the splom we switch the default showlowerhalf = TRUE / showupperhalf = FALSE:

library(plotly.core)

fig2 <- fig |>
  update_traces(showupperhalf = FALSE)

fig2

Each dimension has a property, visible, set by default to TRUE. We can choose to remove a variable from splom, by setting visible = FALSE in its corresponding dimension. In this case the default grid associated to the scatterplot matrix keeps its number of cells, but the cells in the row and column corresponding to the visible false dimension are empty:

library(plotly.core)

dims[[3]] <- go_splom_dimension(
  label = "petal length",
  values = ~petal.length,
  visible = FALSE
)
fig2 <- fig |>
  update_traces(dimensions = dims)

fig2

Splom for the diabetes dataset

Diabetes dataset is downloaded from kaggle. It is used to predict the onset of diabetes based on 8 diagnostic measures. The diabetes file contains the diagnostic measures for 768 patients, that are labeled as non-diabetic (Outcome=0), respectively diabetic (Outcome=1). The splom associated to the 8 variables can illustrate the strength of the relationship between pairs of measures for diabetic/nondiabetic patients.

library(plotly.core)

df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/diabetes.csv")

We define a discrete colorscale with two colors: blue for non-diabetics and red for diabetics:

pl_colorscale <- list(
  c(0.0, "#119dff"),
  c(0.5, "#119dff"),
  c(0.5, "#ef553b"),
  c(1, "#ef553b")
)

Then create the splom:

xaxis_style <- go_xaxis(
  showline = FALSE,
  zeroline = FALSE,
  gridcolor = "#ffff",
  ticklen = 4,
  title = go_xaxis_title(font = go_font(size = 13))
)
yaxis_style <- go_yaxis(
  showline = FALSE,
  zeroline = FALSE,
  gridcolor = "#ffff",
  ticklen = 4,
  title = go_yaxis_title(font = go_font(size = 13))
)

fig <- df |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_splom(
    dimensions = list(
      go_splom_dimension(label = "Pregnancies", values = ~Pregnancies),
      go_splom_dimension(label = "Glucose", values = ~Glucose),
      go_splom_dimension(label = "BloodPressure", values = ~BloodPressure),
      go_splom_dimension(label = "SkinThickness", values = ~SkinThickness),
      go_splom_dimension(label = "Insulin", values = ~Insulin),
      go_splom_dimension(label = "BMI", values = ~BMI),
      go_splom_dimension(label = "DiabPedigreeFun", values = ~DiabetesPedigreeFunction),
      go_splom_dimension(label = "Age", values = ~Age)
    ),
    text = ~ factor(Outcome, labels = c("non-diabetic", "diabetic")),
    diagonal = go_splom_diagonal(visible = FALSE),
    marker = go_splom_marker(
      color = ~Outcome,
      colorscale = pl_colorscale,
      size = 5,
      line = go_splom_marker_line(
        width = 1,
        color = "rgb(230,230,230)"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Scatterplot Matrix (SPLOM) for Diabetes Dataset<br>Data source: <a href='https://www.kaggle.com/uciml/pima-indians-diabetes-database/data'>[1]</a>",
    hovermode = "closest",
    dragmode = "select",
    plot_bgcolor = "rgba(240,240,240, 0.95)",
    xaxis = xaxis_style,
    yaxis = yaxis_style,
    xaxis2 = xaxis_style,
    xaxis3 = xaxis_style,
    xaxis4 = xaxis_style,
    xaxis5 = xaxis_style,
    xaxis6 = xaxis_style,
    xaxis7 = xaxis_style,
    xaxis8 = xaxis_style,
    yaxis2 = yaxis_style,
    yaxis3 = yaxis_style,
    yaxis4 = yaxis_style,
    yaxis5 = yaxis_style,
    yaxis6 = yaxis_style,
    yaxis7 = yaxis_style,
    yaxis8 = yaxis_style
  )

fig
